title: Rank-one purity discharges the finite-determinant hypotheses
statement:
Let $X_0$ be a normal geometrically connected curve over $k_0$, put
$|k_0|=q$, fix $\iota:\Qlb\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathbf C$, and let
$\lambda_\iota(a)=2\log|\iota(a)|/\log q$ be the real weight character
of [d-weights]. Every nonzero lisse Weil sheaf $\mathcal Q$ on $X_0$
has finite geometric determinant in the sense of [d-weights]. If
$\mathcal Q$ is irreducible, then

$$
\dw_\iota(\mathcal Q)=\dw_{\lambda_\iota}(\mathcal Q),
$$

the left side as in [def-wf-determinantal-weight] and the right side as
in [d-weights].

proof.text: Use the finite-field and coefficient conventions of [def-weil-punctual-weights]: $q>1$ and $\ell\nmid q$. By [def-pc-curve], $X_0$ is integral, separated, finite type over $k_0$, and of dimension one, hence pure of dimension one. Put $X=X_0\times_{k_0}k$ and $\Pi=\pi_1(X,\bar x)$. Geometric connectedness makes $X$ connected. These are the scheme hypotheses needed below. In particular $X$ is Noetherian and separated, as required for the coefficient conventions: after extending scalars, a finite affine cover with finitely generated coordinate algebras remains such a cover (the same generators generate $A\otimes_{k_0}k$ over $k$). Apply [pqf-lem-locnoeth-lft] over the Noetherian field $k$ and use this finite cover for quasi-compactness. Separatedness persists since the diagonal is cut out locally by ideals, whose extended ideals cut out the diagonal after scalar extension. Let $V$ be the stalk of the nonzero lisse Weil sheaf $\mathcal Q$, with the geometric action, degree-one operator $T_s$, and Weil action $\rho$ of [def-wf-fundamental-representation].

By [def-pod-lisse-l-adic-sheaves](4), the underlying lisse $\Qlb$-sheaf has a lisse $E$-model for some finite $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$. By [cor-galois-lisse-representations](2), its fibre has a continuous geometric $E$-representation, and extending scalars gives $\rho_{\rm geom}$. Choose an $E$-basis of that fibre. Enlarge $E$ to contain the finitely many matrix entries of $T_s$ and $T_s^{-1}$; each entry is algebraic over $\mathbf Q_\ell$, so adjoining finitely many keeps the extension finite. The identity $T_s\rho_{\rm geom}(g)T_s^{-1}=\rho_{\rm geom}(sgs^{-1})$ in [def-wf-fundamental-representation] then holds over $E$: both matrices have entries there and their equality can be checked in $\Qlb$. By [lem-wf-weil-fundamental-representation], $\rho(gs^n)=\rho_{\rm geom}(g)T_s^n$. Thus this same formula takes values in $\operatorname{GL}_r(E)$ and realizes the Weil representation over $E$. It is continuous: the geometric $E$-action is continuous by the cited equivalence; on each open degree coset it is that action multiplied by the fixed matrix $T_s^n$. No irreducibility or assertion about subquotients is needed here.

source.place: Paragraph 1: finite coefficient field, expanded for this particular sheaf

proof.text: By [def-mg-determinant-line], the rank-one sheaf $\det\mathcal Q$ has character $\chi_{\det}=\det\circ\rho:W(X_0)\to E^\times$. This character is continuous: in the chosen basis its value is the finite determinant polynomial in the continuous matrix entries of $\rho$, and its inverse is the same polynomial evaluated at $\rho(w^{-1})$. Apply [thm-wf-rank-one-finite-geometric-image-curve]. Its curve hypotheses hold by step 1, its coefficient field is the finite $E$ from step 2, and $\ell\nmid q$. It gives that $\chi_{\det}(\Pi)$ is finite. In the Weil degree datum [d-monodromy], $P=\Pi$, so this is exactly finiteness of $\delta_{\mathcal Q}(P)$ in [d-weights]. This proves the first clause for every nonzero $\mathcal Q$, with no assumption of irreducibility.

source.place: Paragraph 1: determinant character and finite geometric image

proof.text: Choose the same degree-one lift $s$ in the Weil degree datum. By [cor-wf-rank-one-punctual-purity-curve], applied to the continuous $E^\times$-valued character of step 3 and the restriction of the fixed $\iota$ to $E$, the determinant line is punctually $\iota$-pure of weight $b=2\log_q|\iota(\chi_{\det}(s))|$. The character value is nonzero because it is a determinant of an invertible operator. Expanding $\log_q$ and $\lambda_\iota$ as in [d-weights] gives $b=2\log|\iota(\det\rho(s))|/\log q=\lambda_\iota(\det\rho(s))$. All hypotheses of the corollary are those already checked in steps 1–3, and an isomorphism $\iota$ is in particular an embedding.

Now assume $\mathcal Q$ irreducible and write $r=\operatorname{rank}\mathcal Q>0$. By [lem-wf-determinantal-weight-exists], there is exactly one real punctual purity weight $a$ of its determinant line. Step 4 supplies such a weight $b$, hence $a=b$. By [def-wf-determinantal-weight] and [d-weights], with the same degree-one lift $s$, respectively $\dw_\iota(\mathcal Q)=a/r$ and $\dw_{\lambda_\iota}(\mathcal Q)=\lambda_\iota(\det\rho(s))/r$. Substitute $a=b=\lambda_\iota(\det\rho(s))$ to obtain the claimed equality. The finite geometric determinant hypothesis in the latter definition was proved in step 3.

source.place: Paragraph 3: uniqueness and division by rank

Step 1: def-pc-curve gives integral, separated, finite type, dim 1, hence pure dim 1; X is Noetherian via pqf-lem-locnoeth-lft (Stacks 01T6) plus quasi-compactness, separated by base change, and l is invertible. These hypotheses match those of def-pod-lisse(4), cor-galois-lisse(2) and thm-wf-rank-one-finite-geometric-image-curve. Step 2: the E-model, plus adjoining the finitely many algebraic entries of T_s^{±1}, gives a continuous Weil representation over a finite E; this is a correct sheaf-specific replacement of the blueprint's loose descent claim. Step 3: det∘rho is continuous, the rank-one theorem gives finite image on Pi, and P=Pi by d-monodromy, so the first clause holds without irreducibility. Step 4: the corollary allows the restricted embedding and gives 2log_q|iota(det rho(s))| = lambda_iota(det rho(s)). Step 5: uniqueness from lem-wf-determinantal-weight-exists gives a=b; both definitions divide by the same rank r>0, so the two weights agree. Edge cases checked: rank one; Qlb(-1); an irreducible rank-2 family with det Qlb(-1); changing s by u in Pi changes det only by a root of unity; reducible sheaves (first clause only).
